item.title: Dysfunctional Functionals and their Therapies in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.00377v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The exchange-correlation functional in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory (TDDFT) is known to have dependence on past densities and initial states, and yet this memory-dependence is ignored in practical calculations which almost always use an adiabatic approximation. We discuss the dysfunction that arises due to this deficiency and point to therapies that go beyond the adiabatic approximation. Still, adiabatic TDDFT has had success in a wide range of systems for response properties and for fully non-equilibrium dynamics, and why this is so is only partially understood. This, together with the rigorous foundation of the exact theory and its favorable system-size scaling, provides tremendous impetus for continuing to strive towards improved approximations to the exact functionals, and a deeper understanding of the impact of approximations in applications.
item.dc:creator: Neepa T. Maitra

item.title: Autonomous Analysis of Thermoelectric Materials Big Data by Multi-Agentic AI and Construction of a Knowledge Base and Specialized AI
item.description: arXiv:2611.00627v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large databases of paper-derived experimental materials data hide essential information on materials. Their analysis is demanding, large-scale and complex, making manual knowledge extraction very difficult. To address this challenge, we developed Multi-Agentic AI (MAA) for automated, autonomous analysis of materials experimental big data and a specialized AI built on the obtained knowledge. MAA's nine role-specific AI agents, under predefined instructions and quality checks, autonomously perform data extraction, compositional feature generation, machine-learning modeling, feature-importance analysis and knowledge-base recording, iterating while inheriting previous knowledge. Delegating numerical processing to code makes large-scale data tractable; recording every choice and result enables later tracing to sources. In four thermoelectric-data experiments varying theme and cycle counts, the knowledge graph grew: knowledge clustered by theme and vocabulary was shared across themes. The specialized AI, searching and reading these records, answered materials questions citing sources. Retrospective verification also revealed errors, traced through the records to their sources.

item.title: Ta-based S-I-S junctions for integrated superconducting electronics
item.description: arXiv:2611.04982v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we have presented S-I-S Josephson junctions with $\rm\alpha$-Ta electrodes and a ${\rm TaO}_x$ barrier. We grew base and top ${\alpha}$-Ta electrodes using seed layer engineering, showing both Nb and ${\rm TaN}_x$ are viable seed layer choices, and particularly emphasize that at room temperature a re-seed layer is required to nucleate $\rm\alpha$-Ta for the top electrode. However, we note that the choice of seed layer can have subtle implications on the electrical tunneling behavior of the junctions. We used room-temperature probing of variable junction areas, combined with Ambegaokar-Baratoff physics, to characterize the wafer scale critical current densities. For 0.4 $\mu$m$^2$ junctions, we found junction spreads as low as 2.0% across the 20 x 20 mm chip relevant for device performance. The entire process was carried out using standard industry foundry processing using 150 mm wafer tooling, which is an important step towards proving that Ta-based junctions can be implemented at scale. We have successfully fabricated and tested junctions with $\rm\alpha$-Ta electrodes and a ${\rm TaO}_x$ insulating tunnel barrier, demonstrating that this is a material platform which merits further investigation and studies for potential application in classical and quantum superconducting technologies.

item.title: Towards Multiscale Molecular Representation Learning through Geometry-Based Fragmentation for Polymer Property Prediction
item.description: arXiv:2611.07998v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It is well established that molecular substructures can contribute unequally to chemical and physical properties, with specific motifs or side chains often playing dominant roles. Fragment-based representations have therefore emerged as an effective strategy for incorporating chemically meaningful inductive biases, as exemplified by molecular fingerprints and fragment-based attention mechanisms. However, many existing fragmentation-based machine learning methods rely on predefined chemical rules, which may yield suboptimal fragmentation for previously unseen or chemically unfamiliar structures and often overlook the importance of multiscale molecular representations. To address these limitations, we formulate molecular fragmentation as a radius-constrained optimization problem inspired by the k-center formulation, where the number of clusters is not fixed a priori but emerges from the specified radius, and propose a geometry-based fragmentation method that partitions arbitrary molecular or material structures using largely geometric information, without relying on predefined chemical fragmentation rules. The method provides flexible control over fragment size, enabling the construction of multiscale fragment representations for scale-adaptive modeling. Building on this framework, we develop a geometric fragment-based attention mechanism that integrates multiscale structural information and incorporate it into a multimodal machine learning model combining p-SMILES representations with three-dimensional (3D) conformational information. Experiments on a benchmark polymer dataset show that incorporating 3D conformational information improves prediction accuracy for several properties over models based exclusively on p-SMILES representations. Explainable artificial intelligence analyses further provide insights into the physical relevance of the learned representations.
